## Structural map engine (`ghx map` / `read --map`)

**Package:** `internal/mapengine/` (Go, no external files needed beyond this repo)

### Entry point / dispatcher
- **`internal/mapengine/types.go`** — `Map(path string, content []byte, opts Options) (Result, error)` (line ~136) is the single public entry point. It normalizes options via `NormalizeOptions` and dispatches by `opts.Engine`.
  - `EngineRegex` → `RegexMapper{}.Map`
  - `EngineTreeSitter` → `mapTreeSitterWithFallback(..., warnUnsupported=true)`
  - `EngineAuto` (default) → `mapAuto(path, content, opts)`
  - any unknown value → falls back to `RegexMapper` with a `Fallback: true` warning

### Per-file engine selection (the "auto" logic)
`mapAuto()` in `internal/mapengine/types.go` (~line 152) selects by file extension:
```go
switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
case ".go":
    // try GoASTMapper{}.Map first; on error, fall back to RegexMapper (Fallback: true)
case ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".py", ".rs":
    // mapTreeSitterWithFallback(path, content, opts, warnUnsupported=false)
default:
    // RegexMapper{}.Map — plain heuristic engine for everything else (java, kt, rb, etc.)
}
```
`mapTreeSitterWithFallback` itself further falls back to `RegexMapper` if `TreeSitterMapper` returns an error (e.g., `ErrUnsupportedLanguage`), so regex is the universal last-resort engine.

### The three concrete engines (all implement the `Mapper` interface in `types.go`)
1. **`internal/mapengine/goast.go`** — `GoASTMapper`, uses Go's own `go/parser` + `go/ast` to extract package/func/type/const/var symbols precisely for `.go` files. Errors out (wrapping `ErrUnsupportedLanguage`) only on unparseable source.
2. **`internal/mapengine/treesitter.go`** — `TreeSitterMapper`, backed by `github.com/odvcencio/gotreesitter` + `grammars` package. Uses `grammars.DetectLanguage(path)` to identify the language, then a per-language `TreeSitterLanguageConfig` (`defaultTreeSitterLanguageConfigs()`, covering go/typescript/tsx/javascript/python/rust) driving a tags-query-based tagger. Some languages (e.g. Go, Rust) are configured to merge in regex-derived symbols (`MergeRegex: true`) for constructs tree-sitter's tag query doesn't catch (imports, package/use statements).
3. **`internal/mapengine/regex.go`** — `RegexMapper`, a line-oriented regex heuristic keyed by file extension (`regexRules` map covering go/ts/tsx/js/jsx/py/rs/java/kt/rb), with a generic fallback rule set (`rulesForPath`) for unlisted extensions. This is the universal fallback engine and also the engine for "everything else."

### Shared result-building
`buildResultFromSymbols` (in `types.go`) is common to all three engines: sorts/dedupes symbols, applies `Kind` filtering, and formats output lines per `Level` (compact/minimal/outline/standard).

### Wiring into the CLI
- **`internal/ghx/read.go`** (~line 187) is the sole caller of `mapengine.Map`, invoked when `opts.Map` is true (i.e., the `read --map` / `ghx map` code path). It passes through user-supplied `Engine`, `Level`, `Kind` options and surfaces `mapResult.Warnings`/fallback info to the CLI output.
- Corroborated by **`docs/adr/0013-ghx-map-command.md`**, which explicitly states: *"`internal/ghx/read.go` calls `mapengine.Map(...)` and has no parser logic."* — confirming the architecture intent that all language-specific parsing lives in `mapengine`, not the CLI layer.

## What I did not verify
- I did not clone/build the repo or run `ghx map` against sample files to confirm runtime behavior — this is based on static reading of source via the GitHub API/`gh` CLI.
- I did not inspect the external `github.com/odvcencio/gotreesitter` / `grammars` dependency's internals (e.g., exact grammar coverage or `DetectLanguage` behavior) — treated as a black-box dependency per `go.mod`.
- I did not check `internal/cli/*.go` for how CLI flags (`--map-engine`, etc.) are parsed into `mapengine.Options` — only confirmed the final consumption point in `read.go`.
- Did not check `regex_test.go` or other tests, so behavior described is from source reading only, not test-verified in this session.
